snippet.title: Archeologists Rebuild The Most Powerful Medieval Fortresses That Changed Civilization
snippet.description:
How Did They Build It? The Mind-Blowing Physics of Medieval Castles

How did medieval engineers construct massive, towering mega-structures capable of withstanding ultra-violence, brutal sieges, and heavy artillery—all without modern machinery or computing power?

In this deep-dive documentary, we go beyond the myths of chivalry to uncover the raw logistics, staggering costs, and ingenious architectural physics behind Europe's greatest fortresses. From quick-built timber mounds to impregnable concentric stone walls, discover how the arms race between castle builders and military strategists shaped the modern world.

The Timber Origins: Why 99% of early medieval castles were actually made of wood, and how the Normans used them to conquer England.

The Pig Fat Secret: The brutal reality of medieval siege warfare, including how King John used 40 fat pigs to collapse an entire stone tower.

The Concentric Revolution: How builders designed "walls within walls" to trap attackers in deadly crossfire.

The Birth of a Title: The political theater behind Caernarfon Castle and how it created the "Prince of Wales" tradition.

From Fortresses to Palaces: How the arrival of gunpowder forced castles to evolve from warlike bastions into luxurious fantasy estates.

snippet.description:
As global temperatures rise, a mysterious chapter of human history is melting out of alpine ice patches in the Yukon and Norway. Unlike moving glaciers that crush everything in their path, stationary ice patches act as ancient deep freezes. Now, archaeologists are racing against time to rescue perfectly preserved 9,000-year-old wooden atlatl darts, feathers, prehistoric clothing, and even human remains before they rot forever. This premium documentary explores the frontlines of climate change archaeology and the profound cultural secrets thawing from the mountain peaks.

snippet.title: She Caught Him Cheating... So He Got Rid of Her (ft. Annie Elise)
snippet.description:
Before Helle Crafts disappeared, she told four different people the exact same thing: "If anything happens to me, do not believe it is an accident."

On November 18th, 1986, the 39-year-old Pan Am flight attendant and mother of three walked into her Newtown, Connecticut home after a transatlantic flight... and was never seen again. Her husband Richard said she'd gone to Denmark for a family emergency. Then he said she'd run off with another man. Police compared her to a stray dog who'd come home when she got tired.

It took her friends, a private investigator, a landfill dig, and a utility worker who remembered a woodchipper on a riverbank at 4 AM to crack the case open.

What they found in that wood chip pile changed Connecticut legal history forever.

Morgan, Kaelyn, and special guest Annie Elise of 10 to Life trace all 10 clues... from the chest freezer Richard bought five days before Helle vanished, to the 2,660 strands of blonde hair recovered from a pile of wood chips, to the tooth fragment that finally put Richard Crafts away... without a body... for the first time in Connecticut history.

snippet.title: Just how ancient is sumo? - Lee Thompson
snippet.description:
Trace the history of sumo, and explore how the sport was designed and modified to reflect ancient Japan’s culture and traditions.

--

Sumo wrestling is known across the world as a beloved form of entertainment, a grand display of strength, and an ode to Japan's ancient past and traditions. But surprisingly, many of these so-called "ancient" traditions were actually recent inventions. So, what were these fabricated practices, and how do they relate to sumo’s true history? Lee Thompson traces the evolution of the sport.

Dig into the vast and wild world of fungi, and explore how these organisms evolved to play a range of essential ecological roles.

The diverse fungal kingdom, which includes everything from baker’s yeast to edible mushrooms to foot infections, has long defied assumptions. Scientists estimate that somewhere between 2 and 12 million species of fungi remain undiscovered— either because they’re microscopic, live hidden within other species, or for other unknown reasons. snippet.title: What happens if you eat a silica gel packet? - Vivian Jiang
snippet.description:
Explore the science of silica gel, and find out why these packets are everywhere and if they're actually dangerous to ingest.

--

Of the many, many things we’re not supposed to snack on, perhaps the most common forbidden food is silica gel. This tiny packet pops up in packaging for everything — from TVs and guitar cases to sunscreen and snack foods. So why is silica gel everywhere, and what would actually happen if you ate it? Vivian Jiang digs into the science of this pervasive product.
